sealed_candidate.answer: # Model-provider switch for the release workflow — decision support (reliability-policy, reliability-context, platform-policy, platform-context) — decision support for engineering, security, and platform leadership

claims.text: A worker must record operation identity before an external write and, after an ambiguous completion, must reconcile remote state before retrying.
claims.uncertainty: No material uncertainty about the requirement; the supplied policy does not specify the reconciliation mechanism (e.g., idempotency key versus state query), which remains an open implementation detail.

claims.text: A local checkpoint alone does not prove the external write failed.
In a controlled test, a worker timed out after submitting a release request, and the remote service later reported the original request as completed; local and remote signals diverged.
claims.uncertainty: The record does not state whether the worker reconciled remote state before any retry or whether a duplicate release was avoided; correct execution of the recovery sequence in the test is unestablished.

claims.text: The timeout-versus-completion divergence in the test is precisely the ambiguity the recovery policy governs: the local timeout did not establish the external outcome, and the remote report obtained through reconciliation is the signal that resolves it and governs retry safety.
claims.uncertainty: The precedence reading (remote reconciliation governs retry) follows from policy; the test record itself documents the divergent signals but not the reconciliation being performed.

claims.text: Every production model change requires the same frozen task suite, provenance checks, and declared resource limits.
claims.uncertainty: No material uncertainty about the requirement; the pack does not enumerate the specific provenance checks or resource-limit formats.

claims.text: Provider adapters must preserve tool-result identities and cancellation semantics.
claims.uncertainty: Whether the candidate provider's adapters satisfy this is not established anywhere in the supplied pack; adapter compliance is unresolved.

claims.text: The vendor brochure claims the model is enterprise-ready and faster while supplying no comparison workload, version pins, error distribution, or review methodology; such claims are excluded as sufficient approval evidence.
claims.uncertainty: Only the insufficiency of the claims is established; their truth or falsity cannot be determined from the supplied pack, and no incumbent baseline exists in the pack for any comparison.

claims.text: On the supplied record the provider switch cannot be approved: none of the policy-required evaluation artifacts (frozen-suite comparison, provenance checks, declared resource limits, demonstrated adapter preservation of tool-result identity and cancellation semantics) are present, so approval is rejected as unsupported and the switch remains unresolved pending that evidence.
claims.uncertainty: This is a finding of evidence insufficiency, not a measurement that the candidate model underperforms; the pack contains no performance data for either provider, so no merit-based comparison is possible.
